To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the association between risk factors for diabetes and incident diabetes differed significantly by case definition and that the association between the metabolic syndrome, insulin, and incident diabetes were stronger for the study protocol case than for self-report case definitions.
the strength of association of incident diabetes with major risk factors differed by case definition.
the magnitude of the relation of risk factors for diabetes with incident diabetes differs by case definition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel risk factors for type 2 diabetes.
the identification of risk factors of incident diabetes using different diabetes case definitions.
the effect of different case definitions on the strength of association for incident risk factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnitude of association of risk factors for incident cases of diabetes depends on the case definition.
the strength of the association between diabetes risk factors and diabetes depends on how diabetes is defined.
the risk factors for incident type 2 diabetes are similar, but not identical, when different case definitions are used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there are differences in the association between risk factors and incident diabetes by case definition, which should be taken into account when designing and interpreting studies of novel risk factors.
the strength of association of traditional risk factors for incident Type 2 diabetes varies according to the diabetes definition used.
the strength of associations between risk factors and incident diabetes differs according to diabetes case definition and fasting glucose screening criteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
case definitions can have a significant effect on the strength of association between risk factors and incident diabetes.
the strength of the association between risk factors and diabetes may vary by case definition and that the use of a single case definition may not be appropriate for all epidemiologic studies.   1

case definitions can influence the association of risk factors with incident diabetes and that the magnitude of the risk associated with a risk factor for incident diabetes may be dependent on the case definition used.
